players.product: Korean OSAT buying Hanmi packaging equipment

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report: consolidated H1 2026 revenue of KRW 60,046 million, up 16% year on year from KRW 51,597 million, with the operating loss narrowing to KRW 2,437 million from KRW 16,044 million and the net loss to KRW 3,724 million from KRW 13,874 million; Q2 alone delivered revenue of KRW 33,513 million and an operating loss of KRW 461 million on a positive gross margin
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue KRW 60,046 million (+16% YoY), operating loss KRW 2,437 million, net loss KRW 3,724 million; Q2 revenue KRW 33,513 million, operating loss KRW 461 million

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 revenue mix: memory packaging KRW 33,367 million (55.57%) with Samsung Electronics named as the leading customer, and non-memory packaging KRW 26,679 million (44.43%) with Broadcom named as the leading customer; exports were KRW 39,069 million (65.07%) and domestic sales KRW 20,977 million (34.93%), with the Americas contributing KRW 13,531 million
quarterly_data.figure: memory packaging KRW 33,367 million (55.57%), non-memory KRW 26,679 million (44.43%); exports KRW 39,069 million (65.07%)

quarterly_data.signal: Packaging lines ran at 19.68% average utilisation in H1 2026 — capacity of 534,163 thousand units (129.02K per hour over 23 hours a day) against production of only 105,124 thousand units, versus 1,098,183 thousand units of capacity and 208,533 thousand units of output in 2025; a large idle-capacity overhang at a Korean OSAT even as AI packaging demand rises
quarterly_data.figure: packaging utilisation 19.68% (capacity 534,163 thousand units, output 105,124 thousand units)

quarterly_data.signal: Technology: Signetics has secured mass-production infrastructure for Recon flip chip, its premium high-value package type, and for Advanced SiP modules, and is investing in and developing LAB (Laser Assisted Bond) technology to win new SiP, large-body and fine-pitch business as devices get lighter and more multi-functional. Its 7nm silicon-node package has completed qualification and is in mass production, the 5nm silicon-node package has completed process and sample development, Cu pillar plus non-SOP packages have been developed to 70/65/60um fine pitch, and 3D AOI detection has been extended from 12um to 4um
quarterly_data.figure: 7nm package qualified and in mass production, 5nm package sample development complete; Cu pillar non-SOP fine pitch to 60um; 3D AOI detection 12um to 4um

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration: three customers each above 10% of revenue contributed KRW 27,634 million, KRW 8,468 million and KRW 7,054 million in H1 2026 — KRW 43,156 million combined, against KRW 26,862 million a year earlier — and are not named in the filing. Signetics carries no long-term supply contracts: order volumes arrive daily and weekly and convert to revenue within a short period, so no separate order backlog is managed
quarterly_data.figure: three customers above 10% of revenue totalling KRW 43,156 million of H1 2026 revenue; no long-term contract backlog

quarterly_data.signal: Raw materials in H1 2026 totalled KRW 40,241 million (USD 26,105 thousand): BGA PCB KRW 27,811 million (USD 18,041 thousand) from Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Korea Circuit, Haesung DS, Simmtech, Daeduck Electronics, Nanya and Kinsus; gold wire KRW 8,511 million from LT Metal and MK Electron; mould compound KRW 967 million from Samsung SDI, KCC, SM Materials and Sumitomo; solder ball KRW 651 million from Duksan Hi-Metal and Alpha Assembly Solutions Korea; and lead frame KRW 176 million from Haesung DS and MHT. Domestic BGA PCB prices rose to KRW 287 thousand per thousand pieces from KRW 216 thousand in 2025 and KRW 186 thousand in 2024, and domestic gold wire to KRW 334 thousand per kft from KRW 235 thousand — package-substrate and gold input costs still climbing
quarterly_data.figure: raw materials KRW 40,241 million; BGA PCB KRW 27,811 million; domestic BGA PCB price KRW 287 thousand per kpcs versus KRW 216 thousand; gold wire KRW 334 thousand per kft versus KRW 235 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Capital spending stayed light: property, plant and equipment additions of KRW 3,117 million in H1 2026 (machinery KRW 1,205 million and equipment KRW 1,487 million) and no significant new facility investment resolved by the board. On 2025 revenue of KRW 103,047 million Signetics held about 0.88% of the Korean packaging market, against Amkor Technology at 44.73%, JCET's STATS ChipPAC Korea at 23.18%, STATS ChipPAC Korea at 10.88%, Hana Micron at 9.00%, ASE Korea at 6.70% and SFA Semiconductor at 3.04%
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 capex KRW 3,117 million; 2025 revenue KRW 103,047 million, about 0.88% of the Korean packaging market

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook: management ties packaging demand to wafer output from Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and TSMC, which must be assembled and tested to end-user specification, and says rising integration and miniaturisation are pushing up packaging difficulty, expensive equipment investment and the need for skilled staff — raising the entry barrier for new players. Signetics is steering away from low-margin, share-losing PDIP and SOIC work toward higher-value FBGA and eMCP CSP-family products, and its expanded flip-chip line is contributing materially to revenue; it is also diversifying with Chinese-region fingerprint-sensor customers Focaltech, Goodix and A-ker and US customers Maxlinear and Movandi through its Santa Clara office
